title: Introducing the Big Words
note: Recognise all eight Big Words from English sentences. Full translation is introduced separately.

title: Names and identity
note: Build a personal pepeha: Names and identity. Reference practice: tōku. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Meet the TAMs
note: TAM recognition first; use familiar actions. Objects with i start in Lesson 8; ki connections start in Lesson 9. Level 2 choices practise TAMs and, from Lesson 9, i/ki; English ongoing prompts accept both taught ongoing forms.

title: Say what someone is not
note: Negate classification using familiar people and animals. No job-title vocabulary. Reference practice: tāku, tōku. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Did not
note: One negative frame at a time, using already introduced actions, objects and singular pronouns. Reference practice: tāu, tōu. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Is not happening
note: One negative frame at a time, using already introduced actions, objects and singular pronouns. Reference practice: tāna, tōna. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Will not
note: One negative frame at a time, using already introduced actions, objects and singular pronouns. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Not yet
note: One negative frame at a time, using already introduced actions, objects and singular pronouns. Reference practice: āku, ōku. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Give a simple instruction
note: Reuse known actions and destinations. Introduce only the command forms kainga and pānuitia; revisit them later in passive sentences. Reference practice: āu, ōu. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say do not
note: Negative instructions reuse the previous command meanings and familiar base verbs. Reference practice: āna, ōna. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask someone to stop
note: Contrast stopping an action with telling someone not to begin; keep vocabulary familiar. Reference practice: tēhea, ēhea. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say how things should be
note: Introduce four useful qualities inside complete wishes and instructions. Tere and kaha return in comparisons. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Speak to and about groups
note: Add plural pronouns to the known negative-past frame. English states number and inclusion; dual forms remain in review. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say who owns it
note: Known books and food, treated as acquired possessions. Introduce N-possession and contracted singular owners. Reference practice: tā tāua, tō tāua, ā tāua, ō tāua. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Homes and transport
note: Use the home/transport relationship for O-possession. Waka is the only new object word. Reference practice: tā māua, tō māua, ā māua, ō māua. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Choose between nā and nō
note: Contrast the two established relationships. A/O labels are teaching context, not immutable dictionary categories. Reference practice: tā kōrua, tō kōrua, ā kōrua, ō kōrua. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say who something is for
note: Move from existing ownership to intended recipients using the same A-context items. Reference practice: tā rāua, tō rāua, ā rāua, ō rāua. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Homes and transport for someone
note: Use the same O-context items and known owners; no fresh vocabulary load. Reference practice: tā tātou, tō tātou, ā tātou, ō tātou. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say it does not belong
note: Apply familiar ehara to both ownership patterns and the same objects. Reference practice: tā mātou, tō mātou, ā mātou, ō mātou. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say it is not for someone
note: Apply the same negative approach to intended recipients; review positive and negative examples together. Reference practice: tā koutou, tō koutou, ā koutou, ō koutou. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Emphasise who did it
note: Introduce agent emphasis with familiar eating, reading and seeing. Keep ownership and actor emphasis distinct. Reference practice: tā rātou, tō rātou, ā rātou, ō rātou. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Emphasise who will do it
note: Change past actor emphasis to future using exactly the same action and object vocabulary. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say it was not that person
note: Negate the identity of the agent, not the occurrence of the action. Include both past and future emphasis. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Bigger and smaller
note: Introduce two comparison words with familiar animals; avoid loading ten new adjectives onto the first comparison lesson. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Faster and stronger
note: Reuse tere and kaha from wishes; introduce no new adjectives. Names practise the personal i a form. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Things you do regularly
note: Introduce habitual ai and ia rā using five familiar actions, rather than only going somewhere. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say what you can do
note: Ability with known actions and objects. Uses the object-before-verbal-comment pattern, with no active-object i. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ability with movement
note: Extend the same ability frame to familiar intransitive actions; introduce no vocabulary. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Say what you cannot do
note: Negate ability while holding the positive ability sentence vocabulary constant. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Put the object first
note: Reuse command forms kainga and pānuitia; introduce kitea. Compare with active sentences already encountered. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Completed passive actions
note: Change only the aspect of known passive sentences; no new verbs or objects. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Future passive actions
note: Use the known future marker with known passive forms; compare who acts with what is affected. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Compare, describe habits and ability
note: Cumulative retrieval across comparisons, habits and ability. No new words or grammar. Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask why something happened
note: Add a why-question frame to established past actions; no new action vocabulary. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask about usual actions
note: Use familiar ia rā to make the habitual reading explicit. Avoid ambiguous present/future English prompts. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask why something will happen
note: Introduce only āpōpō as a time expression; keep the previously practised question frame and actions. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask why something did not happen
note: Negative why questions reuse known negative meanings and familiar verbs; no extra vocabulary. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask when something happened
note: Replace the question focus with past when while keeping the action vocabulary familiar. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Ask when something will happen
note: Future when questions use the same known actions and pronouns. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: If this happens
note: Join two already familiar clauses; vary the consequence. No new content words. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Another way to say if
note: Practise the same conditional meanings with mēnā; change the frame without changing vocabulary. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: If and alternatives
note: Introduce mehemea using the same scenarios, then contrast it with earlier conditional frames in review. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.

title: Questions and conditions together
note: Cumulative why, negative why, when and if sentences. No new grammar or vocabulary. Reference practice: . Recognition revision uses the English-only introduction; translation revision uses earlier translation lessons.
